_note: Per-channel defaults for studio.py. Content keys are top level; everything about how it LOOKS goes under 'style'. Command-line flags still override.
_writer: 'chatgpt' shells out to the Codex CLI authenticated to the existing ChatGPT subscription. 'ollama' is local and free. No separately billed writer API exists. 'auto' tries ChatGPT and then Ollama; pin a backend when it must not switch.
_style: size_div divides the SHORT edge of the frame, so one setting renders the same size in both outputs and a bigger number means smaller text. case: sentence|upper|lower|none. Depth is border + shadow; box draws a solid plate instead and is off. Captions stay up for length/cps seconds, clamped between min_hold and max_hold -- cps 10 is deliberately slower than Netflix (20) or the BBC (~15), because those assume the subtitle is what you are looking at and here the viewer is also watching the game. Anything here can be overridden per caption in a staged overlays.json.
_fonts: Press Start 2P is fixed-cell at about one em per character, so caption LENGTH decides the rendered size more than size_div does. Captions wrap to three lines, so keep them under about 70 characters. Press Start 2P itself is installed by 'bash tools/get_fonts.sh'; 'fc-list' lists every face this machine has.
_voice: OFF by default -- pass --voice, or set voice true here. Chatterbox runs locally and uses its built-in voice unless voice_reference points to a clean WAV you own or have permission to clone. voice_exaggeration controls emotion; start at 0.5.
_timing: Captions land on the exact frame their event was logged -- every value the event scan reads changes as the thing happens. caption_offset shifts all of them by a fixed number of seconds if a whole run reads late or early; it is 0 by default and nothing is adjusted unless you set it.
